learning_objectives: Formulate column and row views of matrix-vector multiplication
Perform Gaussian elimination to find matrix rank and pivots
Compute matrix inverses using Gauss-Jordan elimination

exam.title: MIT 18.06: Linear Systems, Elimination & LU Factorization
exam.description: Undergraduate linear algebra exam covering Gaussian elimination, matrix multiplication views, and LU / PA=LU decomposition.
exam.instructions: Answer all questions rigorously showing all work where applicable. Time limit: 60 minutes.

questions.text: In Prof. Strang's column picture, what does the matrix equation A * x = b geometrically represent?
options: The intersection of n hyperplanes in m-dimensional space.
A linear combination of the column vectors of A, scaled by the components of vector x, yielding vector b.
The projection of vector b onto the nullspace of matrix A.
The determinant of the parallelepiped formed by matrix rows.
questions.correct_answer: A linear combination of the column vectors of A, scaled by the components of vector x, yielding vector b.
questions.rubric: The column picture views Ax as x_1 * col_1 + x_2 * col_2 + ... + x_n * col_n = b.

questions.text: If a 3x3 matrix A has pivots 2, 5, and -3 during Gaussian elimination without row exchanges, what is det(A)?
questions.rubric: When no row exchanges occur (P = I), the determinant of matrix A equals the product of its pivots: 2 * 5 * (-3) = -30.

questions.text: Given a square matrix A, explain why the LU factorization A = LU is computationally preferable to computing the explicit inverse matrix A^(-1) when solving Ax = b for multiple right-hand side vectors b.
questions.correct_answer: LU takes O(n^3/3) operations and solving Ly=b, Ux=y takes O(n^2), avoiding numerical instability and higher flop count of explicit matrix inversion.
questions.rubric: Full marks require stating: (1) Factoring A into LU takes ~2/3 n^3 flops once; (2) Each subsequent solve Ly = b and Ux = y takes only O(n^2) back-substitution flops; (3) Explicitly multiplying by A^(-1) is numerically less stable and more expensive.
